Same commercial fitness photography and normal-to-short-telephoto lens feel. Movement mechanics dictate a new camera/pose; do not copy the incline press pose. No new blue palette, fog, neon, shirtless posing, branding, text, numbers, watermarks, anatomy highlights or gym clutter. One athlete only, natural proportions, neutral focused expression, two anatomically plausible hands with wrapped grips, physically coherent implements and support/contact shadows. Fit the WHOLE athlete, both complete shoes, all weights/bar ends and bench/support feet within the square with about 8% breathing room; action occupies roughly 80–85% of longest image axis, not a tiny figure. Never cut off or merge equipment. Preserve full photographic detail and strong implement/torso/arm silhouette for downscaling.
